title: A Cut Axon Runs a Program

scenes.tts: Cut a mouse nerve. The part of each axon beyond the cut looks normal for about a day. Then it falls to pieces. In one strain of mouse, the same cut axons stay intact for two weeks or more. What is different about that mouse?
scenes.visual: A neuron with a long axon is cut; the stump looks normal, then breaks into beads; a second mouse's stump stays intact with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Cut a mouse nerve. The part of each axon beyond the cut looks normal for about a day. Then it falls to pieces. In one strain of mouse, the same cut axons stay intact for two weeks or more. What is different about that mouse?

scenes.tts: The axon is the long process that carries a neuron's output. The cell body holds the nucleus. People long assumed a cut stump simply starves, like a severed branch. But mice that lack one gene, called Sarm one, keep cut axons intact for a long time. If one mutation can stop the breakdown, something is running it.

scenes.visual: Starving idea chip, then a deleted-gene mouse row beside a normal row; the stump of the mutant stays whole; a program box appears inside the stump.

scenes.tts: Here is how the program starts. An enzyme called N M N A T two works in the axon, and it is short-lived. The cell body must keep sending it down the axon, like trucks refilling a tank. A cut closes the road. The supply stops, and N M N A T two in the stump runs low.
scenes.caption: Here is how the program starts. An enzyme called NMNAT2 works in the axon, and it is short-lived. The cell body must keep sending it down the axon, like trucks refilling a tank. A cut closes the road. The supply stops, and NMNAT2 in the stump runs low.
scenes.visual: Teal NMNAT2 packets travel down the axon; a cut blocks them; the stump's NMNAT2 gauge drains below a threshold line.
scenes.narration: Here is how the program starts. An enzyme called NMNAT2 works in the axon, and it is short-lived. The cell body must keep sending it down the axon, like trucks refilling a tank. A cut closes the road. The supply stops, and NMNAT2 in the stump runs low.

scenes.tts: With N M N A T two gone, its raw material, N M N, builds up. And N A D plus begins to fall. N M N A T enzymes make N A D plus from N M N. A protein called Sarm one waits in the axon, held shut. In the leading model, a rise in N M N, relative to N A D plus, switches it on.
scenes.caption: With NMNAT2 gone, its raw material, NMN, builds up. And NAD+ begins to fall. NMNAT enzymes make NAD+ from NMN. A protein called SARM1 waits in the axon, held shut. In the leading model, a rise in NMN, relative to NAD+, switches it on.
scenes.visual: Two bars: NMN rises, NAD+ falls; a closed clamp-shaped SARM1 sits above them and opens when the ratio tips.
scenes.narration: With NMNAT2 gone, its raw material, NMN, builds up. And NAD+ begins to fall. NMNAT enzymes make NAD+ from NMN. A protein called SARM1 waits in the axon, held shut. In the leading model, a rise in NMN, relative to NAD+, switches it on.

scenes.tts: Sarm one is an enzyme. Once switched on, it cleaves N A D plus. Then A T P falls. As energy fails, calcium rises inside the axon. Calcium switches on calpains, enzymes that cut proteins. The calpains cut the cytoskeleton, and the axon fragments. All of this happens in a stump with no nucleus.
scenes.caption: SARM1 is an enzyme. Once switched on, it cleaves NAD+. Then ATP falls. As energy fails, calcium rises inside the axon. Calcium switches on calpains, enzymes that cut proteins. The calpains cut the cytoskeleton, and the axon fragments. All of this happens in a stump with no nucleus.
scenes.visual: Open SARM1 cuts NAD+ chips; NAD+ then ATP bars drop; calcium dots fill the axon; calpain chips cut the scaffold lines; the axon breaks into beads.
scenes.narration: SARM1 is an enzyme. Once switched on, it cleaves NAD+. Then ATP falls. As energy fails, calcium rises inside the axon. Calcium switches on calpains, enzymes that cut proteins. The calpains cut the cytoskeleton, and the axon fragments. All of this happens in a stump with no nucleus.

scenes.tts: Now the slow mouse makes sense. Its W L D S protein is a longer-lived source of N M N A T activity. It keeps the tank full after the trucks stop. Delete Sarm one instead, and cut axons survive too. So the stump is not starving. It is running a program, and a program has parts that can be stopped.

scenes.visual: The chain supply, NMN/NAD+ sensor, SARM1, collapse across the frame; Wlds feeds the supply step, Sarm1 deletion blocks the SARM1 step, and each leaves the stump whole.
